Findings

1. (factual, BLOCKING) The Nintendo DS partition is not source-verbatim as staged. The registered DS source table shows the second row as `Nintendogs (all versions)` in the Title/Game cell, while the CSV stages `Nintendogs`. This conflicts with the artifact's own active rule that Title cells are taken verbatim from the per-console list page, and it hides the same grouped-row semantics that the artifact carefully preserves for Pokémon Generation I/II. Evidence: `List of best-selling Nintendo DS video games`, list table row 2 (`Nintendogs (all versions)`, 23.96 million, April 21 2005); staged CSV row `Nintendo DS,Nintendogs,23.96,2005`; `curation.json::normalization_decisions[Title]` says titles are verbatim from source. Minimal fix: either change the CSV/key value to `Nintendogs (all versions)` and propagate the exact label through prose, or explicitly redefine the normalization rule away from source-verbatim row labels and justify that departure. The former is cleaner and matches the grouped-title policy already used elsewhere.

2. (factual, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) The active Tetris provenance prose overstates fuzziness relative to the registered value source. The Game Boy list intro says "over 35 million", but the registered row-value table gives `Tetris` a numeric `35,000,000` Sales cell. Active prose in `draft.json::temporal_note`, `curation.json::universe_listing[Tetris]`, `normalization_decisions[Units Sold (millions)]`, and `open_questions` describes the staged `35.00` as a lower-bound extraction from a fuzzy row value. The numeric CSV cell is still supported, so this does not block readiness, but the provenance story should distinguish the exact table cell from the looser intro sentence. Evidence: `List of best-selling Game Boy video games`, list table row for Tetris (`35,000,000`); intro prose on the same page says `over 35 million`.

3. (factual, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) The PS2 within-partition boundary prose is stale. `collection_summary::boundary_row_check` says the fourth-ranked PS2 row is "likely Final Fantasy X ~10.85M"; the registered PS2 list shows the correct fourth row is `Gran Turismo 4` at `11.76 million`, after the staged top three (`Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas`, `Gran Turismo 3: A-Spec`, `Grand Theft Auto: Vice City`). The top-3 CSV rows remain correct, so this is narrative hygiene only. Evidence: `List of best-selling PlayStation 2 video games`, lead + list table lines covering ranks 1-5.

Checks passed

- The 5-console partition universe is correct: PS2, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo DS, Game Boy & Game Boy Color, and PS4 are the top five rows of the console master; PlayStation is correctly outside the N=5 cut. Evidence: `List of best-selling game consoles`, best-selling consoles table rows 1-7.
- Source registration is structurally correct at 6 URLs: one universe master plus five per-console `[universe, ranking, value]` pages.
- The 15-row partition cardinality, 3 rows per partition, composite PK uniqueness, partition sort order, and all other staged numeric values checked correctly against their cited per-console pages.
- Game Boy/Game Boy Color combined-platform handling and Pokémon Generation I/II grouped-title documentation are source-faithful.
